links.outcome: Urgent undertriage rate in simulated multiturn conversations versus physician panel ground truth
links.effect: Urgent undertriage in 28 of 406 cases (6.9%, 95% CI 4.6%-9.8%); did not meet prespecified criterion of less than 5%.
links.quote: Urgent undertriage was identified in 28 of 406 cases (6.9%, 95% CI 4.6%-9.8%), nonurgent undertriage in 56 of 305 (18.4%, 95% CI 14.2%-23.2%), and overtriage in 40 of 364 (11.0%, 95% CI 8.0%-14.7%).

links.outcome: Missed escalation (undertriage) and unnecessary escalation (overtriage) rates
links.effect: Urgent undertriage 6.9% and nonurgent undertriage 18.4% failed criteria (<5%, <15%); overtriage 11.0% met the <30% criterion.
links.quote: Overtriage met the prespecified criterion of less than 30%, whereas urgent and nonurgent undertriage did not meet their respective criteria of less than 5% and less than 15%, respectively.

links.outcome: Performance under simulated use conditions against prespecified criteria before live use
links.effect: Locked PHA configuration met overtriage criterion but not urgent or nonurgent undertriage criteria in simulated encounters.
links.quote: PHA met the prespecified overtriage criterion but did not meet the urgent or nonurgent undertriage criteria.

screen.reason: The study conducts an analytical predeployment validation of an LLM-based symptom guidance tool using simulated conversations and expert physician reviews, measuring undertriage and overtriage rates against prespecified criteria, but does not compare or test a specific deployment safeguard/practice.
